content:
If you've been using apps in the Apple Watch beta this summer, you may have noticed that some existing apps can't open in watchOS 27. Apple has identified the issue and is automatically updating those apps on behalf of developers to ensure compatibility.

These updates will be pushed via the App Store, with the release notes stating: "This app has been updated by Apple to prepare for compatibility with watchOS 27. No new features have been added."

Apple notified developers this week that the entire process will be completed by August 31.

watchOS 27, along with iOS 27 and all the other new operating systems, is expected to be released to the public around mid-September, so the necessary updates are being rolled out in a timely manner.

Apple says it had to do this because of problems with the arm64 architecture portion of some watchOS apps. It appears they are automatically reprocessing and repackaging the affected apps to fix the binary compatibility issues, allowing existing apps to continue working properly without developers having to take any action.
